convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom() to call custom indicator 'i-KlPrice_Vol' which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. Also depends on two external .mqh libraries (TradeAlgorithms.mqh and SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) for trade execution and smoothing algorithms. Custom indicator buffer 3 is the signal source with a proprietary 0-4 color coding scheme. JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA smoothing methods are from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, not built-in.

derived_values.name: Signal strength classification (0-4 scale)
derived_values.used_by: Entry rules and position sizing tier

other_exits: Close long positions when Col[1]==0 (strong sell) or Col[1]==1 (weak sell) and BuyPosClose is enabled
Close short positions when Col[1]==4 (strong buy) or Col[1]==3 (weak buy) and SellPosClose is enabled
Close uses separate magic numbers (Magic1, Magic2) so both tiers of positions are closed independently

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Two-tier sizing based on signal strength: normal signal (buffer==4 buy or buffer==0 sell) uses MM1=0.1 deposit fraction with Magic1=555; strong signal (buffer==3 buy or buffer==1 sell) uses MM2=0.2 deposit fraction with Magic2=777. MMMode determines calculation method: LOT=fixed lot, FREEMARGIN/BALANCE/LOSSFREEMARGIN/LOSSBALANCE=fraction of account.

custom_logic_notes: The EA reads buffer 3 of the custom i-KlPrice_Vol indicator, which outputs a color code 0-4 representing signal strength and direction: 0=strong sell (deep oversold), 1=weak sell (mild oversold), 2=neutral, 3=weak buy (mild overbought), 4=strong buy (deep overbought). Entry requires a transition: for buy signal Col[1] must be at target level AND Col[0] must be below that level (e.g. Col[1]==4 AND Col[0]<4 for strong buy). This means the indicator must have just crossed into that zone, not been already there. Two independent magic numbers allow the EA to track and manage normal vs strong signal positions separately. The indicator works on a separate timeframe (default H8) which may differ from the chart timeframe, making this a multi-timeframe EA. SignalBar=1 means signals are read from the previous completed bar, not the current forming bar. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose flags act as directional permissions. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen_M1, BuyPositionClose_M, SellPositionOpen_M1, SellPositionClose_M functions with built-in position checking and margin verification.
python_conversion_notes: Requires reimplementation of: (1) SmoothAlgorithms.mqh smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) - these are proprietary adaptive smoothing algorithms not available in standard Python libraries. (2) The i-KlPrice_Vol custom indicator logic must be reverse-engineered or obtained separately - it combines volume-weighted price with dual smoothing and outputs a 0-4 color-coded signal. (3) TradeAlgorithms.mqh trade functions (BuyPositionOpen_M1, BuyPositionClose_M, etc.) which handle position checking, margin verification, and order execution - these need manual conversion. The multi-tier magic number system (Magic1 for normal signals, Magic2 for strong signals) means position tracking must filter by magic number. The conditional position sizing (MM1 vs MM2 based on signal strength tier) and MarginMode enum (LOT, FREEMARGIN, BALANCE, LOSSFREEMARGIN, LOSSBALANCE) add complexity. SL/TP values are in points (1000/2000) but no digit adjustment logic is present in the EA itself - the TradeAlgorithms.mqh library likely handles _Point conversion internally. The multi-timeframe design (indicator on H8, EA on any chart) requires careful bar synchronization in Python.
